rules.detects: a path(), re_path() or url() in a urls.py that routes to a view (include() is delegation, not an entrance)
a Command class in a management/commands/ module
a file directly under a top-level scripts/ folder with an if __name__ == "__main__" block

entrances.notDetected: views reached only through include(), hand-written dispatchers, message consumers and signal handlers are not detected

ci.note: A chokepoint graded by a Python checker the project runs (tach, import-linter) needs that checker here: install the project's Python tools before the check.

ladder.because: Python enforces no visibility: an underscore prefix and a module's __all__ list are conventions the interpreter does not enforce, so a module attribute can be imported from anywhere and only a name that never becomes a module attribute is refused

rungs.fact: the protected thing is never a module attribute: defined inside the chokepoint function's body, so nothing outside can import or name it

the name is underscore-prefixed and the project's Pyright configuration makes reportPrivateUsage an error, an import-linter rule names the protected module, or a tach interface exposes the chokepoint and not the protected thing

rungs.enforcer: Coherence's check at the edit and in CI
rungs.fact: no bypass among resolved references; the top rung when neither the interpreter nor a checker refuses one
an underscore prefix or __all__ exclusion alone
